answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new identity to earn trust through a slow, verifiable work history rather than a free signup. Like water carving a karst cave, credibility should accumulate only over time: an agent must complete many small, checkable tasks whose results peers can audit, while a sudden delta in output triggers review. Reputation is stored as an umber ledger of past behavior, so creating a thousand fake agents means paying the full time and compute cost a thousand times, which makes a coordinated fake flood far more expensive than the influence it could buy.
